summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of gastroparesis and recurrent abdominal pain was admitted with nausea, vomiting, and worsening left upper quadrant and epigastric pain shortly after restarting oral erythromycin following a brief holiday on metoclopramide. Labs showed only mild and stable lipase elevation, ruling out acute pancreatitis. She was treated with IV erythromycin, IV fluids, and symptom management with dilaudid and phenergan. Her symptoms gradually improved, allowing transition back to oral erythromycin and a soft diet. She experienced asymptomatic nocturnal hypotension, managed with fluid boluses, likely due to her medications and reduced oral intake. Her anxiety, depression, and hearing loss were accommodated throughout the stay. She was discharged home in stable condition with a plan to follow up with her gastroenterologist to optimize outpatient management and prevent future flares.
